title: BAI Weekly Demo & DT BAU Langdock walkthrough — meeting notes (Aug 12–14, 2026)
content:
Aug 14, 2026
BAI Weekly Demo

Attachments BAI Weekly Demo
Meeting records Transcript Recording 


Summary
The team reviewed the enterprise site update and aligned on integration strategies for construction document management workflows.

Enterprise Site Value Proposition
The updated site clarifies company value through structured document models and improved accessibility. It functions as a funnel for enterprise engagement.

Construction Industry Opportunity Alignment
Construction management represents a key opportunity for high level business intelligence. Reusable document components will standardize workflows across fragmented project data.

Embedding and Integration Strategy
The team decided to integrate high level document models with external platforms to enhance accessibility. Embedding features will allow live documents to exist within 3rd party software.


Next steps
[The group] Provide Site Feedback: Provide feedback on the updated enterprise site and share impressions via Discord.
[The group] Test Site Pitch: Demonstrate the site to diverse technical and non-technical contacts to gauge pitch effectiveness.
[teep - Powerhouse] Update Site Screenshot: Swap the current site hero documentation image with the Privy identity verification screenshot.
[The group] Add Embed Support: Integrate iframe embedding capabilities into the Datab project demo.
[The group] Build Datab Features: Continue developing features requested for the upcoming Datab proposal.


Details
Did the screenshots in this section make your notes better or worse?
Enterprise Site Makeover: Teep - Powerhouse presented an update to the enterprise site, designed to clarify the company's value proposition to both technical and non-technical audiences. The site functions as a funnel to encourage users to book a call for enterprise engagement, though the scheduling feature requires integration with services like Mailchimp before it is fully operational (00:00:00). The platform, Powerhouse, aims to transform sensitive, document-heavy processes by structuring workflows, establishing human-in-the-loop approvals, and maintaining attributable history, specifically addressing the issue of siloed data that limits AI effectiveness (00:01:06). Teep - Powerhouse provided a walkthrough of the site's document model, which treats individual fields within documents as structured data, and expressed a desire to update the site's identity verification section to be more inclusive of non-web3 users (00:03:25).

Site Feedback Request: Teep - Powerhouse invited team members to review the updated site and provide feedback, either directly or via Discord. They encouraged sharing the site with individuals of varying technical backgrounds to test the clarity of the pitch (00:06:42).
Industry Alignment and Construction Use Cases: Wouter - Powerhouse endorsed the site's direction, noting its general applicability across various industry-specific consultancy projects. Drawing on a recent discussion with Datad regarding automated onboarding forms for construction projects, Wouter - Powerhouse highlighted that while many industry tools already handle low-level, specific data, Powerhouse is uniquely positioned to manage the high-level business intelligence and document-heavy project management that often relies on manual, fragmented processes (00:06:42). The construction industry, which involves "nomad" teams and standardized requirements like Building Information Management (BIM) execution plans, represents a significant opportunity where Powerhouse can provide reusable document components that standardize workflows without locking clients into a single proprietary platform (00:09:54).

Speckle Integration Strategy: Wouter - Powerhouse explained the strategy of integrating Powerhouse's high-level document models with low-level, industry-specific data platforms, using the open-source platform Speckle as a model (00:15:57). Speckle facilitates the synchronization of 3D data across various applications like Revit, Blender, and AutoCAD, and offers a robust, mature ecosystem that Powerhouse can leverage (00:18:47) (00:22:09). By combining Speckle’s ability to manage low-level details (such as door counts or piping data) with Powerhouse's high-level document models, the team aims to create a system where documents automatically update when underlying 3D models change, providing significant value without requiring clients to replace their existing software stacks (00:17:17) (00:22:09).

Embeddable Document Functionality: Wouter - Powerhouse proposed implementing an embedding feature, similar to how Speckle allows models to be embedded into Notion, to increase the accessibility and utility of Powerhouse documents. By utilizing the "Iframely" protocol, which provides metadata and standardized rules for embedding web content, Powerhouse could allow users to copy-paste URLs to embed live, interactive document editors into third-party platforms like Notion, Miro, or SharePoint (00:25:08) (00:27:14). This approach addresses the needs of network-based organizations where different stakeholders use varied, existing systems, thereby allowing Powerhouse to integrate into workflows with low friction and support organic growth (00:32:23).

Revenue Strategy and Upcoming Schedule: Wouter - Powerhouse noted that the user feedback meeting regarding the Datad proposal was moved to the following Tuesday (00:33:50). The team plans to continue building features relevant to Datad's needs in the interim. Wouter - Powerhouse emphasized that leveraging mature, external software like Speckle allows the team to offer high-value consultancy services in the short term, thereby balancing immediate revenue generation with the longer-term development of a scalable product (00:35:41).

Aug 12, 2026
Powerhouse × DT BAU — Langdock walkthrough
Invited Apeiron - Powerhouse Wouter - Powerhouse ah@dtbau.com
Attachments Powerhouse × DT BAU — Langdock walkthrough
Meeting records Transcript Recording 


Summary
The session explored leveraging artificial intelligence for Building Information Modeling and automated documentation to solve data fragmentation challenges.

Leveraging AI and Automation
Centralized AI interfaces and language models facilitate automated onboarding and task creation. This approach successfully bridges manual gaps in data management and administrative processes.

Addressing Fragmented Data Silos
Unstructured data across disparate platforms creates significant barriers to operational efficiency. Establishing structured data flows for tasks, metadata, and site information remains the critical priority.

Unified Platform Integration Strategy
Evaluation of existing industry-specific software tools will precede any development of custom integration solutions. This strategy facilitates the transformation of unstructured documentation into machine-readable datasets for improved assessment.


Decisions
Aligned
Prioritize existing software solutions The project adopts a strategy to prioritize existing software solutions over custom development to avoid unnecessary reinvention of the wheel.

We've updated the Decisions section using your feedback.
Let us know what you think: Helpful or Not Helpful


Next steps
[Agli Hysi] Share IFC file: Share an example file of the IFC properties specification document.
[Agli Hysi] Analyze Past Incidents: Investigate historical project retrospectives to identify specific instances where improved IT or AI integration could have prevented issues.
[Agli Hysi] Evaluate Plannerly: Analyze the tool and share feedback regarding its potential to enhance current project workflows.
[Agli Hysi] Send AIA Document: Forward the template currently used for project processes to the team for analysis.
[Wouter - Powerhouse] Review BIMQ: Assess BIMQ Neo functionality to determine if it meets project requirements and data structuring needs.
[Agli Hysi] Share BIM Properties: Compile and share the list of BIM properties currently requested from project stakeholders.
[Agli Hysi] Review Plannerly: Evaluate the features of Plannerly and provide feedback on its overall utility for current projects.
[Agli Hysi] Share Lessons Learned: Forward documentation regarding project retrospectives and identified lessons learned.
[Agli Hysi] Recommend Tools: Identify and send information about additional software tools relevant to the discussed processes if found.


Details
Did the screenshots in this section make your notes better or worse?
DT BAU Role and Langdock Adoption: Agli Hysi, representing DT BAU, describes their work in Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digitization, aiming to improve project efficiency for clients. They utilize Langdock as their primary AI and automation tool because it is hosted in Germany and provides access to multiple language models, such as OpenAI and Gemini, in a single package (00:00:58).
Langdock Interface and Capabilities: The platform serves as a central chat interface where users can select various language models, view token usage, and upload data—including PowerPoint and Word templates—to be vectorized for AI agent building (00:02:29). Users can integrate this with SharePoint for data retrieval, and Agli Hysi demonstrates how easily these agents can be constructed to assist project members with specific data questions (00:04:12).
Data Integration and CDE Challenges: Integration with SharePoint is currently limited to DT BAU's internal environment due to stakeholder access restrictions (00:05:52). Agli Hysi notes that while they are familiar with Common Data Environments (CDEs) like Dialog, Katenda, Autodesk, and Squirrel, platforms like Dialog are difficult to integrate because they are closed systems with limited API capabilities (00:07:31).
BIM and Semantic Data Transition: The industry is shifting from 2D DWG files to 3D BIM models, with Revit serving as the primary tool for generating semantic information. While DWG files are still used for 2D exports and precise measurements, the goal is to build 3D models first and derive plans from them, ensuring that elements—such as doors—are properly tagged with semantic data (00:11:26) (00:14:11).
Project Documentation and Standards: DT BAU supports the maintaining phase of buildings by helping stakeholders define and apply correct semantic data structures, often referencing BIM standards (00:18:17) (00:20:44). Two primary documents shape these projects: the BIM Abwicklungsplan (BAP) and the Exchange Information Requirements (EIR), which dictate roles, processes, and necessary digital data (00:27:50).
Cost Management Digitization: While DT BAU is not directly involved in financial approvals, they are digitizing traditional cost management processes. By taking data from complex, non-semantic Excel tables used by stakeholders, they create dashboards to visualize project costs more effectively (00:34:07).
Hardware and Software Constraints: The project environment is 90 to 95 percent Windows-based, largely because Revit and many other construction industry tools lack support for Mac operating systems. Consequently, Mac users in architecture studios often resort to using DWG files as an interchange format to work within the Windows-dominated system (00:35:39).
Langdock Workflow Automation Example: A notable workflow in the Novo project involves a public form used to register project participants (00:41:07). Data from this form is added to an Excel database, which triggers task creation in Microsoft Planner and sends automated onboarding emails, demonstrating how Langdock and related tools streamline otherwise manual project management tasks (00:42:41).

Task Management and BCF: The team manages two distinct types of tasks: organizational tasks, tracked via Microsoft Planner, and model-based tasks, which utilize the BCF format (00:47:54). DT BAU tracks these BCF tasks and visualizes trends through dashboards, though they do not create or sign off on them, delegating that responsibility to architects and engineers (00:49:27).
Automation Tool Strategy: The team utilizes a combination of Langdock for AI and language model integration, Microsoft Power Automate for connecting within the Microsoft environment, and formerly N8N (00:55:13). Langdock is favored for its AI integration, while Microsoft Power Automate is preferred for specific triggers like Microsoft Forms (00:57:25).

Onboarding Automation: Agli Hysi explains that the current onboarding process involves sending a link for a check; once completed, the information updates an Excel sheet automatically (00:59:26).

AI Agent Skill Implementation: Agli Hysi introduces the "skills" feature in Langdock, which functions similarly to context by enabling AI agents to execute active processes (00:59:26). They demonstrate a skill created by Data Consulting for HR onboarding that integrates with Microsoft Planner to create tasks for new colleagues. When asked by Apeiron - Powerhouse whether agents can use skills outside their defined scope, Agli Hysi explains that if skills are well-described, agents can successfully identify and utilize them based on user input keywords (01:01:06).
Integrated Project Platform Vision: Agli Hysi outlines a vision for an integrated platform that connects project members, tasks, and 3D model quality checks, moving away from fragmented systems (01:03:57). Wouter - Powerhouse notes the current distinction between fine-grained model tasks in BCF flow and project management tasks in Microsoft Planner, while mentioning ongoing work on a project overview dashboard (01:05:23).
Documentation and Methodology: Wouter - Powerhouse asks if DT BAU focuses on methodology rather than technical model content, given the high volume of documentation work (01:05:23). Agli Hysi confirms that document creation and editing consume a large portion of their time, and they aim to connect different tools into a single system to streamline quality checks rather than reducing tool usage (01:06:56).
Evaluation of Plannerly: Wouter - Powerhouse suggests using Plannerly for documentation and templates and asks Agli Hysi to evaluate it. Agli Hysi mentions they have heard of the tool but have not explored it deeply, though they recognize the potential benefit of making documents machine-readable to support automated BIM checks (01:08:43) (01:11:30).

BIM Model Structuring: Agli Hysi describes the necessity of breaking 3D models into smaller "part models" (e.g., architectural, engineering, electrical) as required by the BIM Execution Plan (BEP), which are then combined in a Common Data Environment (CDE) for collision checking (01:13:06).
BIM Management Role: Agli Hysi clarifies that while they perform some collision checking as part of their BIM management responsibilities, deep collision analysis is typically conducted by the architects or engineers (01:14:28).
Stakeholder Collaboration in Projects: Agli Hysi explains that project organization varies by type, noting that Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) projects involve multiple disciplines working together from the beginning, including clients, construction masters, and consultants (01:15:53).
Maturity Assessment and Workshops: At the start of a project, Agli Hysi conducts assessments and workshops to ensure all stakeholders have a shared understanding of BIM processes and tool usage, relying on internal templates and best practices that are continuously optimized based on project lessons (01:18:55).
Use of Master Templates: Agli Hysi discusses the use of master templates, such as the Exchange Information Requirements, which are customized for specific infrastructure projects to define goals, milestones, and software requirements—specifically looking for IFC compatibility as certified by Building Smart (01:21:45).
Collaborative Documentation Process: Wouter - Powerhouse and Agli Hysi discuss the iterative nature of creating documents like the BEP, which requires continuous stakeholder communication rather than solitary work (01:25:02). Agli Hysi highlights that in IPD projects, these documents are discussed and agreed upon collectively, contrasting this with traditional projects that may suffer from conflicts (01:27:36).
IPD Incentives: Agli Hysi notes that IPD projects include financial incentives where cost savings are shared among participating companies, which encourages team collaboration and collective document management (01:28:55).
Managing Documentation Consistency: Agli Hysi explains that they try to minimize redundant work by centralizing information, such as using the BEP as a primary source (01:30:05). Regarding collision management, Agli Hysi adds that the CDE allows for live updates; when a wall or door is modified based on a BCF task, the information propagates without requiring manual updates to multiple documents (01:31:25).
IT Integration and Retrospectives: Wouter - Powerhouse suggests reviewing past retrospectives to determine if better IT or AI integration could prevent recurring issues, as many current tasks suffer from missing information or improper tracking (01:32:50). Agli Hysi agrees to check internal lessons-learned data to identify areas where technology could improve project outcomes (01:35:50).
Data Silos and Unified Overview: Agli Hysi identifies the fragmentation of data across various tools—such as the CDE, Microsoft Planner, and Mural—as a primary challenge, creating a need for a unified system to maintain a clear project overview (01:34:18).
Software and Regulatory Restrictions: Wouter - Powerhouse inquires about software restrictions (01:37:01). Agli Hysi explains that projects often have strict requirements regarding data sovereignty, noting that some software, such as Autodesk Forma, may be prohibited if the technology or hosting is not based in Europe (01:38:41).
Regulatory Compliance: When asked if regulatory compliance processes are part of their checklists, Agli Hysi clarifies that this is managed by architects and the main client, though they acknowledge it is a significant cost area that could theoretically be automated (01:40:26). Wouter - Powerhouse expresses surprise that this is not currently integrated, given its impact on project costs (01:41:43).
Unstructured Data as a Barrier: Agli Hysi emphasizes that beyond data silos, the primary issue is that the data itself is unstructured, which hinders efficiency (01:44:33). They cite Risk Management as an example, which is currently managed via disconnected Excel tables rather than a standardized, machine-readable process (01:47:05).
Measurable Risk Management: Regarding risk management, Agli Hysi explains that risks are measurable (e.g., based on site plans or delivery schedules) but are not currently gathered in a structured way that reaches higher project management levels (01:48:44).
Dependency Graph and AI Monitoring: Wouter - Powerhouse proposes using AI to create a dependency graph of project tasks to monitor for bottlenecks or missing information. Agli Hysi agrees that having structured access to all project data would enable more efficient and proactive management (01:51:40).
Priorities for Structured Data: When asked to prioritize three types of structured data for the system, Agli Hysi lists: 1) Tasks, 2) Documents and model metadata (with strict access control), and 3) "BIM-to-field" data connecting construction site progress to the digital environment (01:54:25).
Project Setup and Onboarding: Agli Hysi is currently focusing on setting up projects from a technical perspective to prepare for a September start date. This process involves configuring the Common Data Environment (CDE), establishing user roles, creating general documentation, and implementing automated workflows to ensure a smooth project launch (01:57:11). Agli Hysi clarifies that while they handle project management office data management, tasks such as security reviews and user access cleanup are typically managed by the client-side Project Management Office (01:58:59).
Document Management and Scope: Apeiron - Powerhouse requests clarification regarding where Architecture Information Requirements (AIR) and Building Information Modeling (BIM) Execution Plan (BEP) documents fit within the discussed data models (02:00:10). Agli Hysi confirms that these documents serve as the regulatory framework for managing stakeholder needs, as well as controlling document access, visibility, and editing permissions (02:01:43).
Data Strategy and Business Intelligence: Wouter - Powerhouse defines their role as transforming unstructured data into structured data to support business intelligence. They express an interest in building a platform that integrates various workflows to remove data silos and reduce reliance on tools with excessive licensing costs (02:02:55). Wouter - Powerhouse notes that their technology is local-first, emphasizing data protection and the potential to facilitate work within complex construction industry networks where stakeholders often use diverse and rigid software (02:04:17).
Platform Integration and Technical Restrictions: Wouter - Powerhouse discusses the difficulties in customizing third-party Common Data Environments (CDEs) to meet specific project needs due to infrastructure and security limitations. As an example, they state that platforms like Langdock restrict the installation of custom agents or software (02:05:54). They suggest that their own local-first technology offers the necessary flexibility to develop tailored software solutions, provided that specific use cases are clearly identified (02:07:18).
Utilizing Large Language Models for Document Processing: Wouter - Powerhouse proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate tasks such as scanning analog documents into structured digital data and analyzing project images (02:07:18). They emphasize that for these models to provide relevant assessments, they require access to specific project data, such as project planning or BIM issues (02:08:46). The objective is to use this technology to assist with review work that is often neglected due to time constraints (02:10:00).
Leveraging Existing Tools for Structured Data: Wouter - Powerhouse suggests that their existing backup solution can be integrated to extract structured data from key documents like the BIM Execution Plan (BEP). By classifying documents and identifying requirements, they aim to create automated checklists, while noting they want to avoid "reinventing the wheel" if suitable tools are already available (02:11:19).
Software Evaluation and Market Alternatives: Agli Hysi demonstrates two tools that align with these objectives: Plannerly and BIMQ Neo (02:12:24). Agli Hysi explains that BIMQ Neo manages project phases, BIM use cases, and information requirements, while another tool, "Build BIM Permit," bridges the gap by checking models against building regulations based on Information Delivery Specifications (IDS) (02:13:38).
Research and Future Coordination: Wouter - Powerhouse reiterates the importance of identifying concrete use cases and verifying if existing tools can solve them before developing new solutions (02:15:06). Agli Hysi commits to providing a list of BIM properties requested of stakeholders, sharing thoughts on Plannerly, and providing access to retrospectives and lessons learned by Friday (02:17:22). Wouter - Powerhouse notes that once the analysis is complete, they hope to conduct an in-person workshop, acknowledging that the team is distributed across locations including Munich, Nuremberg, and Berlin (02:18:27).
